text: “Be careful that you don’t do your charitable giving before men, to be seen by them, or else you have no reward from your Father who is in heaven.
label: Matthew 6:1

text: Therefore when you do merciful deeds, don’t sound a trumpet before yourself, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may get glory from men. Most certainly I tell you, they have received their reward.
label: Matthew 6:2

text: But when you do merciful deeds, don’t let your left hand know what your right hand does,
label: Matthew 6:3

text: so that your merciful deeds may be in secret, then your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.
label: Matthew 6:4

text: “When you pray, you shall not be as the hypocrites, for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen by men. Most certainly, I tell you, they have received their reward.
label: Matthew 6:5

text: But you, when you pray, enter into your inner room, and having shut your door, pray to your Father who is in secret, and your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.
label: Matthew 6:6

text: In praying, don’t use vain repetitions, as the Gentiles do; for they think that they will be heard for their much speaking.
label: Matthew 6:7

text: Therefore don’t be like them, for your Father knows what things you need, before you ask him.
label: Matthew 6:8

text: Pray like this: ‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.
label: Matthew 6:9

text: Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done, as in heaven, so on earth.
label: Matthew 6:10

text: Give us today our daily bread.
label: Matthew 6:11

text: Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors.
label: Matthew 6:12

text: Bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. For yours is the Kingdom, the power, and the glory forever. Amen.’
label: Matthew 6:13

variants.reading: the doxology is absent (the prayer ends at 'deliver us from the evil one')
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Matthew' records 'Text omitted' for the doxology in א (Sinaiticus), B (Vaticanus), D (Bezae), Z, 0170, f1, the Latin and bo cop traditions and fathers incl. Tertullian and Origen. Codex Washingtonianus (W) stands with the manuscripts that include the doxology (E G K L W Δ Θ Π Σ f13 ... Byz), the reading the WEB prints.

text: “For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
label: Matthew 6:14

text: But if you don’t forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
label: Matthew 6:15

text: “Moreover when you fast, don’t be like the hypocrites, with sad faces. For they disfigure their faces, that they may be seen by men to be fasting. Most certainly I tell you, they have received their reward.
label: Matthew 6:16

text: But you, when you fast, anoint your head, and wash your face;
label: Matthew 6:17

text: so that you are not seen by men to be fasting, but by your Father who is in secret, and your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you.
label: Matthew 6:18

text: “Don’t lay up treasures for yourselves on the earth, where moth and rust consume, and where thieves break through and steal;
label: Matthew 6:19

text: but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust consume, and where thieves don’t break through and steal;
label: Matthew 6:20

text: for where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
label: Matthew 6:21

text: “The lamp of the body is the eye. If therefore your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light.
label: Matthew 6:22

text: But if your eye is evil, your whole body will be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in you is darkness, how great is the darkness!
label: Matthew 6:23

text: “No one can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other; or else he will be devoted to one and despise the other. You can’t serve both God and Mammon.
label: Matthew 6:24

text: Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life: what you will eat, or what you will drink; nor yet for your body, what you will wear. Isn’t life more than food, and the body more than clothing?
label: Matthew 6:25

text: See the birds of the sky, that they don’t sow, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns. Your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren’t you of much more value than they?
label: Matthew 6:26

text:
“Which of you, by being anxious, can add one moment
to his lifespan?
label: Matthew 6:27

text: Why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow. They don’t toil, neither do they spin,
label: Matthew 6:28

text: yet I tell you that even Solomon in all his glory was not dressed like one of these.
label: Matthew 6:29

text: But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which today exists, and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, won’t he much more clothe you, you of little faith?
label: Matthew 6:30

text: “Therefore don’t be anxious, saying, ‘What will we eat?’, ‘What will we drink?’ or, ‘With what will we be clothed?’
label: Matthew 6:31

text: For the Gentiles seek after all these things; for your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.
label: Matthew 6:32

text: But seek first God’s Kingdom, and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.
label: Matthew 6:33

text: Therefore don’t be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Each day’s own evil is sufficient.
label: Matthew 6:34

statement: Almsgiving (tzedakah) was a recognized religious duty among Jews, customarily performed publicly.
label: Almsgiving as a religious duty

statement: Giving in the Temple courts was connected with trumpet imagery: thirteen trumpet-shaped collection chests (shofarot) stood there.
label: Trumpet-shaped offering chests (shofarot) in the Temple

statement: The word 'hypocrites' (hypokritai) literally meant stage actors, and theatres stood in Roman Galilee (e.g. at Sepphoris).
label: Hypocrites as stage actors; theatres in Galilee

statement: Prayer and almsgiving were performed publicly in synagogues and at street corners, standing.
label: Public prayer and almsgiving in synagogues and streets

statement: Houses had an inner room (tameion, a storage chamber) where one could pray in private.
label: The inner room (tameion) of a house

statement: Gentile (pagan) prayers were characterized by much speaking and repetition.
label: Pagan prayer by much speaking and repetition

statement: Jesus taught his disciples a model prayer (the Lord's Prayer), fixed enough to be prayed as given.
label: The Lord's Prayer as a taught form of prayer

statement: The WEB text of Matthew 6:13 closes the prayer with the doxology 'For yours is the Kingdom, the power, and the glory forever.'
label: The doxology at the end of the Lord's Prayer

statement: Fasting was a recognized religious practice, and some fasters made their fasting visible on their faces.
label: Fasting and its visible display

statement: Anointing the head with oil was a normal grooming practice.
label: Anointing the head with oil as grooming

statement: Wealth was laid up in goods subject to decay and theft: garments, metal objects and household stores.
label: Laying up treasure in goods on earth

statement: Stored garments were consumed by moths and stored metal by rust.
label: Moth and rust consuming stored goods

statement: Thieves broke into houses by digging through the wall (mudbrick or earthen construction).
label: Thieves digging through house walls

statement: The eye was conceived as the lamp of the body, in keeping with ancient ideas of vision and light.
label: The eye as the lamp of the body

statement: Slaves served a household master in the Roman world, and a slave could not serve two masters.
label: Serving a master: slavery in the Roman world

statement: Mammon (Aramaic mamona) was a common Aramaic word for wealth and possessions.
label: Mammon: an Aramaic word for wealth

statement: Food, drink and clothing were the constant daily concerns of ordinary households.
label: Daily concern for food, drink and clothing

statement: Farmers sowed, reaped and gathered produce into barns, while birds of the sky live without sowing, reaping or barns.
label: Sowing, reaping and barns; birds without farming

statement: Wild flowers ('lilies of the field') grew in the fields of Galilee.
label: The lilies of the field

statement: Solomon was proverbially arrayed in glory and wealth.
label: Solomon in all his glory

statement: Households baked in clay ovens fuelled with dried grass and other dried plants.
label: Clay ovens fuelled with dried plants
